request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [Name]

Age: 80 years

Sex: Male

Medical Record Number: [Number]

Date of Admission: [Date]

Date of Discharge: [Date]

Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted to our hospital due to the incidentally discovered rectal tumor. The biopsy sample revealed that the 3 cm diameter tumor was a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. Imaging studies showed that the tumor invaded into the muscularis propria, and lateral pelvic lymph nodes were not enlarged. The patient also had a huge benign prostatic hypertrophy, with a size of 85 × 80 × 70 mm.

To achieve complete tumor removal with negative margins, a hybrid transabdominal-transanal approach for ISR was performed. The procedure involved laparoscopic mobilization of the left colon and transabdominal approach up to the anterior dissection of the rectum. Subsequently, a transanal approach was used to complete the dissection procedure. The bilateral pelvic splanchnic nerves were identified at the 5 and 7 o’clock positions. Due to the perineal body and the enlarged prostate, the proper dissection layer at the anterior side was difficult to identify. However, the dissection plane between the rectum and the prostate was identified, and the procedure was completed along the same plane with the assistance of the laparoscopic approach.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and had an uneventful postoperative course. The patient was discharged home on [Date] with scheduled follow-up appointments.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Plan:

The patient is advised to follow-up with his oncologist and urologist for monitoring and further treatment as per their recommendations. The patient is also advised to make diet changes and exercise regularly to maintain good health.

Clinician:

[Name], [Title]

Attending Physician:

[Name], [Title]

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
Principal diagnosis category: **C20**

1. **Condition chiefly responsible for the admission.** The patient was admitted for a rectal tumour. Biopsy confirmed it as a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. It was treated with intersphincteric resection (ISR) using a hybrid transabdominal-transanal approach.
2. **What is not the principal diagnosis.** The benign prostatic hypertrophy made the anterior dissection harder and needs urology follow-up. However, it was not the reason for the admission, so it is a secondary condition.
3. **Chapter letter.** Adenocarcinoma is a malignant neoplasm, so the chapter is **C**.
4. **Category digits.** The primary site is the rectum. Rectal malignant neoplasm is category **C20**.

CODE: C20
